articles.title: Nations League roundup: Portugal mauled by Denmark as Norway sink Wales
articles.summary: Portugal thrashed 4-1 at home by Denmark. Wales bottom of Group A4 after 3-1 loss. Portugal were hammered 4-1 by Denmark on Saturday, an embarrassing Nations League defeat in their first match without Cristiano Ronaldo following his retirement from international football.
body: Rasmus Højlund starred with a superb double as Denmark moved into second place in Group A4 and closed in on a spot in the quarter-finals with an exceptional display in Braga.
Denmark are on nine points from five fixtures, three behind Portugal who were already sure of qualification for the last eight having won all four of their previous group fixtures.

Ahead of kick-off Portugal paid tribute to Ronaldo, who announced his exit from the international game last week, with the team and mascots walking out wearing Ronaldo’s No 7 and his name on their jerseys.
Denmark were the better team from the first minute and it was no surprise when the visitors took the lead from Pierre-Emile Højbjerg’s penalty in the 43rd minute.

articles.title: Andreeva sweeps past Pegula to reach WTA Finals title match after hot-mic controversy
articles.summary: Russian teen beats American 6-3, 6-4 at Indian Wells. French Open champion, 19, assures world No 2 ranking. The rise of Mirra Andreeva has seemed inevitable ever since she burst on to the tour as a precocious 15-year-old more than three years ago, but this week, six months after her maiden grand…
body: A year ago, Andreeva surprisingly failed to qualify for the WTA Finals, missing out by a paltry six points after bizarrely deciding not to compete in the final tournament week before the event. The world No 3 has been utterly supreme in her long-awaited debut appearance, bulldozing through elite opposition to reach the final without dropping a set. She has conceded just 18 games in four matches this week, including a 6-4, 6-0 demolition of the No 1 seed Aryna Sabalenka, winning 11 games in succession from 1-4 down.

Andreeva will rise to No 2 in the WTA rankings for the first time in her career on Monday regardless of the outcome here. The world No 1, Elena Rybakina, and No 3, Aryna Sabalenka, will both be defending a large number of points at the Australian Open after Rybakina defeated Sabalenka in this year’s final, which means the No 1 ranking will almost certainly be a realistic target for Andreeva at the start of the 2027 season, particularly if she closes out this imperious week with a title. She will face the winner of the second semi-final between Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova and Elina Svitolina.

articles.title: The 'manager's dream' who has put NI one game from history
articles.summary: After scoring his first international goal in the 1-0 win over Ukraine, Northern Ireland boss Michael O'Neill says Terry Devlin is "a bit of a dream" to manage.
body: When Terry Devlin picked the ball up on the edge of the area in the 68th minute against Ukraine there was only one thought in his mind.
And when the ball flew into the corner Windsor Park erupted at another highlight of a Nations League campaign that has been a real feel-good story so far.

Heading into Saturday's game they had yet to concede a goal, but the one thing they had lacked was a home win - or even a home goal - after drawing blanks in stalemates with Hungary and Georgia in Belfast.

They had already come close when Jamie Donley slotted home in the first half but the forward had strayed offside, leaving the moment the hosts had been waiting for to come through Devlin's superb winner.

articles.title: Georgia football recruit Marcellus Young Casario dies at 18 after medical emergency
articles.summary: Canadian lineman died Friday after medical incident. Three-star prospect committed to Georgia in June. High school postpones game as coach pays tribute. Marcellus Young Casario, an 18-year-old Canadian high school football player who had committed to Georgia, died Friday following what his school…
body: Casario, a senior defensive lineman at Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School in northeast Georgia, was taken to hospital after an incident Friday morning. The school announced his death later that day but did not identify him until Saturday. No further details about the circumstances were released.
“Rabun Gap immediately followed our emergency response protocols, and local emergency personnel responded, transferring the student to the hospital,” the school said in a statement.
The school postponed its state semi-final playoff game against Cannon School scheduled for Friday night.

Originally from Halifax, Nova Scotia, Casario moved to Georgia to pursue a college football scholarship. The 6ft 5in, 255lb defensive lineman committed to the Bulldogs in June after receiving offers from several major programs.

articles.title: Clara Luvanga strikes as Washington Spirit beat Utah to reach third straight NWSL final
articles.summary: Tanzanian scores second-half winner in 2-1 victory. Spirit reach fifth NWSL final and third in succession. Washington will chase second title at home ground. Clara Luvanga scored her second goal of the postseason in the 57th minute, capitalizing on an errant pass as the Washington Spirit reached…
body: Luvanga raced on to Nuria Rábano’s ill-advised ball after it rolled past Utah center-back Tatumn Milazzo, then chipped it delicately over the advancing goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn for the winner.
It was her fourth goal in all competitions since her September transfer from Saudi club Al-Nassr.

“We didn’t have too much time to work with her, but she’s doing amazing,” Washington coach Adrián González said. “Learning so quick. Knowing what the team needs from her and what this league demands.”

Luvanga also played a crucial pass to create Sofia Cantore’s eighth-minute equalizer for the No 3-seeded Spirit, who will seek their second championship on home turf after being awarded hosting rights in June.

articles.title: Sabalenka apologises & says viral comment 'not directed at Svitolina'
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka apologises and denies claims she insulted opponent Elina Svitolina after a viral clip showed her swearing during her WTA Finals defeat by the Ukrainian.
body: A video of world number two Sabalenka angrily gesturing and swearing in Russian during her 6-3 3-6 6-1 defeat by Ukraine's Svitolina was posted on social media on Saturday.
Some commentators interpreted Belarusian Sabalenka's comments as an insult towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general.
Sabalenka later wrote on social media that "my comment was not directed at Elina" but she lost her temper because of the behaviour of some fans.
"I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment," the 28-year-old wrote.

articles.title: Littler opens bid for third Grand Slam crown with stunning Greaves win
articles.summary: Luke Littler started his pursuit of a Grand Slam of Darts hat-trick with a commanding 5-2 victory against Beau Greaves in Wolverhampton on Saturday night.
body: In a Group A blockbuster, 'The Nuke' struck seven maximums and a 109.97 average to defeat the Women's Matchplay champion.
Littler has yet to taste defeat in 15 Grand Slam matches, as he bids to join Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen by becoming the third player to win three successive titles in the West Midlands.
Greaves had memorably beaten Littler in the semi-finals of last year's World Youth Championship, but the back-to-back world champion had revenge on his mind.

After looking invincible in the first half of 2026 as he won the first five majors, Littler had come up short at the World Series of Darts Finals, then slipped to a first-round exit at the Grand Prix before another last-eight defeat in the European Championship.

articles.title: Ireland shake off sluggish start to brush aside Fiji
articles.summary: Ireland recover from a sluggish first-half performance to wear down spirited Fiji and keep alive their hopes of topping the Nations Championship northern hemisphere table.
body: After thumping Argentina last week, Ireland failed to click in an unconvincing opening, with Tommy O'Brien's early try and a Robert Baloucoune double enough for a 17-15 lead.
Fiji arrived in Dublin without a win in nine previous meetings against their hosts, and having been thrashed 54-17 by France last week.
But they dreamed of a historic win after tries from Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato, and a Ben Volavola penalty, kept them firmly in the contest at the break.
However, Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter and O'Brien crossed as Andy Farrell's men scored 26 unanswered second-half points to deny the Pacific Islanders, who remain without a point in the competition.

articles.title: Devlin nets first international goal as Northern Ireland beat Ukraine
articles.summary: Terry Devlin's first international goal kept Northern Ireland top of their Nations League group as a 1-0 win over Ukraine set up a promotion decider away to Hungary on Tuesday.
body: The 23-year-old Devlin has been in the goals for Portsmouth this term with four, and opened his Northern Ireland account with a fine strike in the 68th minute as he left Ukraine goalkeeper Anatoliy Trubin flat-footed with a shot from distance.

Pierce Charles then made a superb save to deny Danylo Sikan at the death and preserve Northern Ireland's fifth straight clean sheet - the first time they have achieved that since 2017 - and ensure they remain the only side in the competition yet to concede.

The three points put Northern Ireland back on top of Group B2 after Hungary's 2-0 win over Georgia earlier in the afternoon, and ruled Ukraine out of contention as they lost three straight matches for the first time in six years.

A draw in Budapest would be enough to elevate Michael O'Neill's young side to League A, while even in defeat they would face a play-off in March, and they have also earned a pot two place in next month's Euro 2028 draw.

body: The result ensured that, no matter how the closing contests in Group B play out, Austria sealed promotion to League A.
Ireland enter Tuesday's critical home clash at the Aviva Stadium in third place, with one point fewer than their final opponents, Kosovo.
Heimir Hallgrimsson's men were not without chances, but only Kalajdzic made one count when he broke the deadlock in the 79th minute.

articles.title: Veteran Pitcher Goes On Unhinged Rant About MLB Owners As Lockout Nears
articles.summary: The MLB Players' Association and the owners are trying to agree on a new collective bargaining agreement. The current CBA expires on Dec. 1, so the two sides need to figure something out fast.
body: The league posted a video on X of Morgan Sword, the executive vice president of baseball operations, outlining what the owners are proposing, explaining why they think it's right and why the players should agree. The league is clearly trying to garner some fan support for their cause. However, veteran pitcher Jameson Taillon replied to the video, calling out the greed of the owners.

"This is comically bad," Taillon wrote. "They’re being very careful and selective of what they’re saying/showing and how they’re delivering it. This is going to be ugly if they’re trying to sway fan/public support weeks before they even lock us out. At the end of the day- they want to drive down salaries and put more money in the pockets of billionaires. Nobody wins except them. Simple as that. It’s not about competition. It’s never been about competition for them, it just is a nice cover up."

Sword outlined the payroll disparity between big-market and small-market teams, noting that it is harder for small-market teams to win, and saying that over time, teams that spend more win more. He outlined some other issues as well, but the salary cap and salary floor proposal was the main point of the video.

articles.title: Tuchel unhappy as anti-racism protocol questions overshadow Spain clash
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel insisted his words had been "twisted" as questions over anti-racism protocols overshadowed the build-up to England's Nations League showdown in Madrid.
body: Tuchel was asked after England's win over Croatia on Thursday how he and England would react if racist abuse occurred during Sunday's game against Spain.
The head coach responded by saying he would "maybe take five minutes" to remind his players of the anti-racism protocols. Tuchel also said "we will not expect" any abuse to occur in Madrid.
The game is England's first visit to the Spanish capital since 2004, when the match was marred by racist abuse directed at England's black players.
Spain were also fined and handed a partial stadium closure last month as punishment for Islamophobic chanting in Barcelona during a game against Egypt in March.

articles.title: Scarlett Schremmer disqualified from LPGA debut due to illegal green-reading book
articles.summary: Miami sophomore Scarlett Schremmer has been disqualified from the Annika driven by Gainbridge at Pelican for using a green-reading yardage book during competition. Schremmer, who was making her LPGA debut, shot 69-74 to miss the cut.
body: "Schremmer violated Model Local Rule G-11, which, per the LPGA Rules of Play Card, is in effect during all LPGA Tour competitions, except at off-site local qualifying events. This Model Local Rule requires that players are limited throughout their round to using only the yardage book that has been approved for use in the competition."
The LPGA first learned of the potential violation on Thursday but didn't take action until photo evidence was provided on Saturday.

LPGA veteran Perrine Delacour played alongside Schremmer in the first two rounds and, prior to teeing off in Round 3, posted a comment on the Instagram account of Ryan French, better known on social media as "Monday Q Info."
"Can we talk about the yardage [book] illegal and LPGA trust the sponsor invite over 2 LPGA players and 2 caddies," Delacour wrote in a comment on French's post.

articles.title: Schuylerville gallops off with another Section 2 Class C football championship
articles.summary: CLIFTON PARK - The year and the head coach may be different for the Schuylerville football team, but the precision, physicality and results remained the same for the Black Horses, as another Section 2 Class C Super Bowl appearance led to another championship for the program.
body: While Schuylerville was met with some resistance early on against Hoosick Falls/Tamarac, the Black Horses' vaunted rushing attack eventually obtained ample real estate - led by junior standout Ernie DaCosta.

A three-year star, DaCosta rushed for a season-high 233 yards and four touchdowns, as Schuylerville secured its third straight sectional title with a 36-2 victory over the Wildcats at Shenendehowa's Steuerwald Stadium.
"This feels great, man. It feels awesome, for sure," said DaCosta about winning Schuylerville's eighth sectional championship.

Nick Richard, who played at Schuylerville and previously served as an assistant coach, took over the program from John Bowen this season. The fourth-ranked Black Horses (10-1) registered another lopsided win Saturday, as they have now outscored their opponents 516-110.
